verdict.rationale: Checkout.com is a payments processor, so machine-readable settlement and reconciliation reporting is a fair question for this kind of product. The evidence pack never mentions settlement files, reconciliation reports, or a reporting API covering interchange, fees, or network adjustments. The nearest items are real-time visibility into multi-currency balances and earning a share of issuing interchange revenue; both are adjacent features, not reconciliation artifacts.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I get machine-readable reconciliation artifacts — daily settlement files or report APIs covering interchange, fees, and network adjustments — that my finance stack can consume automatically
